\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{न्हावणो} (nhāvṇo)}{न्हावणो (nhāvṇo)}]{\mw{न्हावणो} (nhāvṇo) — to bathe}

\label{lesson:MW-C103-nhavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for someone, then the Marwadi for each.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{न्हावणो}}
\textbf{\mw{न्हावणो}} — \emph{nhāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to bathe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{न्हावणो}} (\emph{nhāvṇo}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{snāti}, \textquotedblleft{}bathes\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry (CDIAL 13786); the match is through Hindi \emph{nhānā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{पकावणो} (pakāvṇo)}{पकावणो (pakāvṇo)}]{\mw{पकावणो} (pakāvṇo) — to cook}

\label{lesson:MW-C103-pakavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for each, then the Marwadi for to bathe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{पकावणो}}
\textbf{\mw{पकावणो}} — \emph{pakāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to cook\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{पकावणो}} (\emph{pakāvṇo}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{pakva}, \textquotedblleft{}cooked, ripe\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{pākaï} under it (CDIAL 7621). The Old Marwari row means \textquotedblleft{}becomes ripe\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\mw{पकावणो}} (\emph{pakāvṇo}) is its causing form, \textquotedblleft{}make cooked\textquotedblright{}. The root is \emph{pac}, \textquotedblleft{}to cook\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\textbf{\mw{बणावणो}} — \emph{baṇāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
CDIAL gives no Marwari row for \textbf{\mw{बणावणो}} (\emph{baṇāvṇo}), \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{}. It lists Old Awadhi \emph{banāvaï}, \textquotedblleft{}makes\textquotedblright{}, and Hindi \emph{bannā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be made\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{vanati}, \textquotedblleft{}desires, gains, makes ready\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11260), and notes a rival account from Sanskrit \emph{varṇayati}, \textquotedblleft{}describes\textquotedblright{}. The match is through those languages.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{जोड़णो} (joṛṇo)}{जोड़णो (joṛṇo)}]{\mw{जोड़णो} (joṛṇo) — to join}

Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to make, then the Marwadi for to break.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{जोड़णो}}
\textbf{\mw{जोड़णो}} — \emph{joṛṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to join\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{जोड़णो}} (\emph{joṛṇo}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*yoṭayati}, \textquotedblleft{}joins\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants. CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{jōḍaï} under it (CDIAL 10496). CDIAL builds it on \emph{*yuṭati}, \textquotedblleft{}is joined\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
